descriptor.scene: Three friends close around a map, seen CLOSE: the camera sits just over the ENGINEER's near shoulder in the lower right foreground, his charcoal-hooded back and shoulder softly out of focus and cropped by the frame, his lap and legs outside the picture. Across from him, sharp and warmly lit by a lantern set on a crate, MAYA leans in on the left pointing at the map, and CHRISSY, mid-laugh in the middle, presses a small pencil cross onto it. The map between them is hand-drawn: trail lines, small crosses for dead ends, a few pencil circles, NO readable words. Evening jungle behind them is soft dark green bokeh. Three people, one lantern, one honest map.
descriptor._caption: So she stops searching alone. She finds Chrissy, who lights up when she has something to share, and the engineer, who says plainly what he knows and what he does not. They draw their maps honestly, dead ends and all, and they keep one rule: whoever finds it tells the others first.
negatives: readable letters, words or numbers on the map
the engineer's face or chest visible in the near foreground

Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal. Identity of record; wardrobe and features exactly as the locked sheets. the-jungle exactly as its reference plate: A vast emerald wilderness of giant-leafed trees, buttress roots, hanging lianas and layered green depth, crossed by narrow hand-cut trails. Warm shafts of daylight drop through the canopy. Above the canopy, in open sky, floats the island the hopefuls are trying to reach; from most of the jungle floor it is hidden by leaves. The jungle is dangerous in an adventurous way, never a horror way: steep gullies, thorn walls, false trails, sudden rain. Interior scenes hold the camera low among the leaves, close to the trail, with green depth stacking behind the subject in soft layers. To show the island from inside the jungle, break the canopy open above a clearing rather than thinning the trees everywhere. Giant leaves, buttress roots, lianas, ferns, moss, cut stakes marking trails, an occasional canvas camp with warm lanterns far off. No ruins, no temples, no animals with screen presence, no signage, no lettering anywhere. The trees are cathedral-tall: a standing adult reaches roughly the height of a buttress root's shoulder, and the canopy closes far overhead. Trails are one person wide. TELL THEM APART, keep every face and hairstyle distinct: maya is the one with half black half white founder, sage olive blazer single button notch lapel sleeves pushed to elbow, white crew neck tee, stone khaki chinos never blue jeans, laptop under arm; chrissy is the one with white woman, long wavy blonde hair worn down center parted past the shoulders, warm wide open bright smile, relaxed cream or white blazer over a simple top default; engineer is the one with black man, short cropped hair and a neat short beard, rounded dark glasses, charcoal grey zip hoodie over a plain tee default. THE ONLY CHARACTERS IN THIS IMAGE ARE: chrissy, engineer, maya. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. Do not add any other person, figure, creature, robot, animal or bystander, whatever the style description above may suggest. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, readable letters, words or numbers on the map, the engineer's face or chest visible in the near foreground. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
